 Show Most recent Most popular Over and out published at 19:00 GMT 19:00 GMT 
 That's your lot for today.
 Good wins for Liverpool, Bournemouth and Newcastle but a desperate defeat for Manchester United, which leaves them contemplating yet another managerial change.
 We'll be back tomorrow as the winner of this year's Ballon d'Or is announced before EFL Cup action to enjoy midweek. See you then!
 24 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How things stand published at 18:59 GMT 18:59 GMT 
 That's almost it from us.
 Eight games into the 2026-27 season and here is how the table is looking.
 Liverpool's win over Brighton lifts them to third, just a point behind the Seagulls, while Bournemouth's thrashing of Manchester United takes the Cherries up to 13th with Michael Carrick's side down in 16th.
 Newcastle are into the top half after victory at Crystal Palace, while Sunderland stay bottom after their draw with Leeds.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 20 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Mixed emotions standing on the touchline' published at 18:57 GMT 18:57 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, speaking to BBC MOTD: "A tough day - the boys went into the game with the best intentions They found it difficult today - bit of tension, anxiety and a bit unsure. It made it difficult.
 "The two goals before half-time put us in a challenging position. The next goal then is important and I could feel the fans wanting to get behind us even at half-time I could feel the noise and willingness to get us forward. I spoke about that at half-time.
 "If we got that at that point then the whole dynamic would be changed but we couldn't get that at the point. Third goal finished the game in many ways. Mixed emotions - you could feel the boys trying to do the right things but you could feel the emotion in the stadium too and it was very mixed feelings for me standing on that touchline.
 "The free-kick against Ayden [Heaven] when he only tackled the ball, there was no one he tackled but the referee gave the free-kick. The free-kick we need to defend better. Leny [Yoro] slipped, he's bitterly disappointed. He's learning and he's made one mistake today. That won't affect him, he's a top player. The wind takes the ball and it's a good finish from the third."
 On leaving Bruno Fernandes on the bench: "He's fit and available but we decided to pick the team that we did today. Unfortunately for everyone we didn't manage to get the right result."
 "We want to push forward and create more, we could've done certain things but not enough really and that's pretty clear."
 19 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'No drama, no panic' published at 18:56 GMT 18:56 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Sunderland 
 Sunderland boss Regis le Bris, speaking to Sky Sports: "It's a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.
 "It's still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it's a new challenge for us and we need to embrace it. I think we showed this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today."
 On their attacking threat: "Good chances but we still need to be clinical. We had this conversation at half time about this consistency and this belief we need to have because sometimes it's just a click and you score but today wasn't the case."
 On seeing belief in his side: "Absolutely. We saw Sunderland on the pitch today so I am confident with the team spirit and confident with the way we are working hard together to get better and consistency is still key. We have another game on Wednesday then Coventry and the objective is to get better."
 On Nordi Mukiele, after the defender went off injured: "He's OK - no problem." 
 On managing different competitions: "This is what we want to be. We want to play in Europe as regularly as possible so facing this challenge is new for us, and you need to learn, you need to create something new and it takes time. No drama, no panic and we are in this situation we expected to be. 
 "Obviously it's still difficult to lose games but we think we are in the right way."
 20 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:56 GMT 18:56 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Jamie Carragher 
Former Liverpool defender on Sky Sports 
 Manchester United need to make that [managerial] change tonight, they need to make that decision.
 The fans have taken the side of Michael Carrick and it's not about him being the manager, it's about him being a huge figure in United's history.
 Those players have done nothing compared to teams of the past so Michael Carrick is always going to win that fight with Bruno Fernandes, and rightly so, no matter how talented a player he is.
 But also, Manchester United as a football club, one of the biggest in the world, are 16th in the Premier League right now and that can't continue. Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight - not just for the good of Manchester United, but also for the good of Michael Carrick.
 It's not nice watching him walking around the stadium at the end, he's really hurting and what's happening right now is not good for United and not good for Carrick.
 22 49 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'They deserve to get booed' published at 18:55 GMT 18:55 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Clinton Morrison 
Former Crystal Palace striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 On the crowd booing after Michael Carrick had left the pitch: 
 That says everything to me. They're with Carrick, the fans, but they're not with the players. Wow. That was alarming. 
 Carrick got a big cheer but as soon it was just the players, they got booed. But they've not been good enough and they deserve to get booed. There's only so much a manager can do. 
 The players are not good enough, in my opinion, to win football matches. 
 67 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:54 GMT 18:54 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Of course, the result that most people will be talking about came at Old Trafford where Manchester United were beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth.
 Michael Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes after his comments midweek and, while his players were roundly booed, the manager had his name sung by the fans.
 The fact remains that Carrick is now under huge pressure and it remains to be seen whether he can hold onto his job.
 11 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We needed this win at home' published at 18:51 GMT 18:51 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, speaking to Sky Sports: "We needed this win at home to celebrate it with the supporters. We had a really good performance from the players. We started really aggressively, and we needed this start. We were very focused on starting well and scoring the first goal. 
 "It feels good and we have to keep going. I am liking a lot of things I am seeing on the pitch. Some of the players had better performances but it is a team you can trust. 
 On Florian Wirtz: "If they give him the ball or not, he has given us the goal. It is not just about the numbers. It is about being better with him on the pitch. Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle; it doesn't look big but we'll see.
 "We had good match-ups and with the speed Barcola has, playing in behind, we have more speed. 
 "I want all the players available. The ones that are close - Dom, Victor. We need these players."

 Post published at 18:51 GMT 18:51 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 You know what, you can't argue with that from James Trafford. The wind was extremely windy.
 42 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The wind was obvious extremely windy' published at 18:50 GMT 18:50 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford, speaking to Sky Sports: "The wind was obvious extremely windy, the conditions were a bit mad to be honest. It was one of those games where both teams were fighting and we had some chances at the end."
 On how he managed the conditions: "I just had to try and hit the ball a bit flatter, but the wind was all over the place, sometimes it went long and it held up. It was mad but it was the same for me and Roefs."
 On keeping his clean sheet: "I am obviously pleased and it it a product of trying to win every day. The more days you win the better chance and position it puts you in to play well, so I just try and win the day."
 On what it is like playing for Leeds: "I have really enjoyed playing week-in and week-out and it's amazing playing for Leeds and feeling the love from the lads, I am enjoying it and so is everyone else."
 Next steps for Leeds: "We need to score more and concede less. We are trying every day to improve that."
 40 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Maybe I'm just an interesting guy' published at 18:48 GMT 18:48 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton 
 Liverpool 
 Image source, Getty Images Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz speaking to BBC MOTD: "We had the right mentality today to go into this game. In the first half or first 30 minutes, we were on top of them and really good in the duels, creating a lot of chances. It's good to end the half and we defended good. Really happy about that."
 On Pascal Gross own goal: "He would've preferred the goal was given to me but it's like this. It was a good moment for us to take the lead in a game. I'm happy that I could be involved in this goal."
 "It's really enjoyable. I think many things weren't so good in the last month so I'm even happier that it's going well at the moment. We are in a good way to get where we want to be. We should keep going like that and I'm happy about that."
 On his ankle injury: "I think it should be alright. It's not too bad. I don't know much yet, we have to check it but it won't be long."
 On people talking about him: "Maybe I'm just an interesting guy. I just play my football. If people want to talk about me or judge me, then that's their job."

 'Very happy to be back' published at 18:46 GMT 18:46 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle 
 Newcastle striker William Osula, speaking to BBC Radio Newcastle: "Absolutely, very happy to be back.
 "Thank God I'm back on the pitch injury-free and blessed now. So yeah, it was really important to get the three points, but also happy to be back in the team now and being able to help with that goal." 
 23 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We had plenty of chances' published at 18:44 GMT 18:44 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, speaking to BBC MOTD on what his side could've done better: "Scored goals. 
 "We started the game, we had a big chance with Yasin that we didn't score. Liverpool scored from easy chances. We had plenty of chances. I saw a Liverpool team with great defencers so we have to give credit to them as well. We tried to go again and kept trying. 
 "We can even control the game more. We focus on the team performance and have to learn and make it better the next time. It's a missed opportunity. 
 "You have to deal with it but after a game, you're never happy. You want to win games, so we are very disappointed."
 17 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'It was a needed win at home' published at 18:42 GMT 18:42 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, speaking to BBC MOTD: "It was a needed win at home. We wanted to have a good performance and finish with the clean sheet. We started strong. In transitions in the first half, we were being aggressive in the duels. We have done our job. 
 "We have had to come back and it becomes more difficult. You need to start strong, score the first goal. We did it today. 
 On Alexander Isak scoring again: "I don't really care how scores the goals but he has the chances normally.
 On keeping a clean sheet: "Especially against Brighton. We know them very well, but overall, we had to defend some crosses and set plays. We were very solid. 
 On Florian Wirtz's injury: "He had a twist on his ankle. it doesn't look very bad but we play every three games. I don't know if he will be available for the next one. 
 On Ronald Araujo: "He deserves the praise. Even in the first goal, he arrives and gives the assist. I am very happy for him."
 35 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The table always reflects where people should be' published at 18:40 GMT 18:40 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Sunderland 
 Sunderland midfielder Luke O'Nien, speaking to Sky Sports: "I think the wind played a big part and credit to both defences and the attacks as well to be able to keep it to no goals in that swirling wind.
 "I think it was a good effort from everybody so obviously we want three points from where we are in the table but keep putting up the performances like that and we'll get some."
 On keeping a clean sheet against Dominic Calvert-Lewin: "As a defender it's always nice to have a clean sheet and especially after the last few games where we haven't had one.
 "It's always something we're looking to do and Robin [Roefs] came up with some big saves, Omar [Alderete] coming on was really good as well and I hope my teammate's [Nordi Mukiele] OK as well because I think that was kind of my fault. But we got the clean sheet for him so hopefully not too bad."
 On being bottom of the Premier League table: "I think always the table reflects fairly where teams deserve to be, and I think over the course of the course of the season if we keep putting in performances like that it will represent where we should be. 
 "But the table always reflects where people should be but we need to keep looking at ourselves, don't look at other anyone else, it's no-one else's fault but us and we know that."
 On playing in Europe: "I think the extra games help - you build momentum, more players come in, it builds rhythm. We've got a game Wednesday, then Saturday, Thursday - as kids growing up all you wanted to do was play football every day.
 "It suits us all nicely and we're going to need everybody in the squad and whatever competition it is we're out there to win games."

 Figure caption, Highlights: Osula and Barnes give Newcastle victory at struggling Palace
 By Neil Johnston BBC Sport football reporter at Selhurst Park Newcastle United secured a much-needed win at Selhurst Park to pile pressure on Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage. 
 After a drab first half low in quality, Newcastle raced into a 2-0 lead after scoring twice in 11 minutes to secure a third top-flight win under Matthias Jaissle. 
 William Osula's first-time finish from Jacob Murphy's 47th-minute cross set the Magpies on their way before Harvey Barnes finished well to double the lead and spark a chorus of boos from frustrated home fans.
 Lukas Hornicek saved well to keep out Adam Wharton and substitute Dario Osorio.
 But Palace, who had been the better team in the first half, crumbled after Osula marked his first start since the opening weekend of the season with his first goal since May.
 The Denmark forward took his goal really well as Newcastle won at Selhurst Park for the first time in six years when Steve Bruce was in charge.
 Palace had made a lively start but with Jean-Philippe Mateta and Daichi Kamada both having attempts, but the problems are mounting for Sage. 
 The Frenchman is only four months into a three-year contract but has now presided over five defeats in eight Premier League games.
 Pressure grows on Sage as fans turn on Palace boss 
 Published 3 hours ago 
 Have your say on Crystal Palace's performance 
 What did you make of Newcastle's display? 
 Palace analysis: What now for Sage? 
 Figure caption, Sage post-match interview - Crystal Palace vs Newcastle
 Palace actually started this game well but it was the same familiar outcome after failing to make their dominance count.
 They are 17th in the table on seven points from eight games, while they have now conceded 12 goals in their past four league and European matches.
 The new manager always had big shoes to fill following the departure of Oliver Glasner, who delivered an FA Cup, Conference League title and Community Shield.
 There were boos at the full-time whistle and it remains to be seen how much time Palace will give the former Lens boss, with this result coming a week after the humiliating 5-0 defeat at fierce rivals Brighton.
 Palace have two away London derbies next - at Fulham in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, and at improving Tottenham on Saturday.
 Ando: 'Still work to be done' after win v Palace 
 Newcastle analysis: Confidence returns after timely win 
 Figure caption, Jaissle post-match interview - Crystal Palace vs Newcastle
 This was a timely win for Jaissle, who was starting to feel the heat himself after three defeats in the previous four Premier League games.
 The German made five changes to the side that lost 1-0 at home to Aston Villa last weekend and, after an uneventful first half, his team sprang into action after the interval.
 Dan Burn, who has been injured, marked his first Premier League start of the season with a solid performance, while the confidence returned to the team after Osula's goal.
 "Today we went for more experience and leadership skills," Jaissle said afterwards.
 "It was a tough game especially in the first half. But the second half was much better and we threatened the opposition more.
 "If we are all together - this journey can be successful."
 Newcastle started the weekend in 11th spot but this win lifted them to seventh before the late match between Sunderland and Leeds.
 They have back-to-back games against Everton next - away on Thursday in the Carabao Cup before hosting David Moyes' side in the Premier League on 2 November.
 The question is, will they use this result as a springboard to kick on?
